episode.subject: spiny leaf insect
episode.title: What met my foot
episode.body: When I had just hatched, I reached past the edge and found nothing. Then the wind pressed against my foot. For one hopeful moment I thought it had come to hold me. I leaned.

imageReview.verdict: Author pass for exact early-stage image and reaching pose; root must judge fictional wind pairing
imageReview.visible: Orange head, short antenna, thin legs, curled abdomen and forward-reaching foreleg are clear. The nearest supporting surface ends along a dark edge. Warm light makes the small body legible against green-gold blur; no distracting text or human equipment dominates.
imageReview.limits: The exact dark substrate is not established as a leaf or branch, so the body says edge only. No visible wind measurement, subsequent lean or fall. Those temporal sensations/actions are fiction. This is a captive photograph, not a documented event at the fictional Australian home. The still must not be described as proof of falling or gliding.

proposals.proseAssessment: Author pass as a brief embodied misreading. The new hatchling mistakes pressure on a searching foot for support and acts on the hope. The lean supplies a consequence rather than an explanatory moral. It neither threatens an audience nor confuses leaf camouflage with food. Root may hold if the implied action is too slight or the still too static; no admission is presumed.

canon.chronology: Opening explicitly places this before adult courtship/feeding and before the later juvenile molt and handling memories. Present adult body does not turn orange or return to first instar. The older recollection implies survival; do not add a documented fall or injury.
canon.appearance: First-instar orange head and dark narrow body are a species-supported early appearance, not an adult morph switch.
canon.home: Woodland near Brisbane, Australia, -27.44, 152.95, unchanged. Cologne is provenance only.
canon.relationships: No new individual or fictional named wind entity introduced.

proposals.fictionBoundary: Interior hope, tactile interpretation, wind and subsequent lean are original fiction. Photo documents the animal, early appearance and reaching posture. No claim of insect psychology, parental support or wind bearing body weight as fact.

biologySources.section: Life Cycle and Spiny Leaf Insect
biologySources.supports: Newly hatched Extatosoma tiaratum have red heads and dark ant-like bodies; later stages become green or brown leaf mimics. Used for chronology and morphology only, not precise emergence duration or an assumed history inside an ant nest.
Primary photo-specific species identification, first-instar description and visible pose; two matching current identifications. Casual because captive, not represented as research grade.

holds.title: Into the green
holds.body: The water closed over my back and cooled every place the sun had found. I sank a little farther. My neighbor was already under, except for his nostrils. I wanted to ask how much of himself he had managed to forget.
holds.reason: The body returns to warmth, withdrawal and abstract forgetting without a distinct payoff. The source animals also have marked pale nodular surfaces requiring a fresh individual-appearance review. Do not casually assign a skin condition or recolor Calder.

holds.title: The patient edge
holds.body: When I had just hatched, I reached past the edge and found nothing. I kept the foot there. For a moment I thought the world might grow a little farther if I waited.
holds.verdict: Hold earlier draft; superseded for proposal by 165-01, literal text preserved here
holds.reason: Waiting alone offers no consequent action. The proposed body adds the mistaken tactile invitation and her lean instead of explaining a lesson.
